modelAnswerFeedback.bestPossibleAnswer: Database indexes (primarily B+ Trees) optimize read query latency from an O(N) full table scan down to an O(log N) tree traversal. However, every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE requires the storage engine to synchronously update every index tree associated with the table on disk and potentially trigger leaf page splits. This causes write I/O amplification, higher lock contention, and larger WAL log generation, which degrades write throughput when tables are heavily indexed.

questionByQuestionAnalysis.bestPossibleAnswer: Database indexes (primarily B+ Trees) optimize read query latency from an O(N) full table scan down to an O(log N) tree traversal. However, every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE requires the storage engine to synchronously update every index tree associated with the table on disk and potentially trigger leaf page splits. This causes write I/O amplification, higher lock contention, and larger WAL log generation, which degrades write throughput when tables are heavily indexed.
